IF YOU WANT TO WRITE SQL LIKE A SENIOR ENGINEER, STOP SELECTING STAR.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES: 1/5

Name your columns, always.

SELECT * breaks when schemas change and drags dead weight over the wire. Explicit beats lazy. 2/5

Filter early with WHERE, not HAVING.

WHERE cuts rows before grouping. HAVING cuts after. Same result, wildly different cost. 3/5

Index what you filter and join.

Check EXPLAIN before and after. One composite index has saved more weekends than any ORM. 4/5

I post daily breakdowns like this for backend, SQL, and interviews.

Follow @owlsky17 so you don't miss the next one. 5/5

IF YOU WANT QUERIES THAT SCALE PAST A MILLION ROWS, STOP NESTING SUBQUERIES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 MOVES: 1/5

JOIN beats subquery in the SELECT list.

Correlated subqueries run once per row. A JOIN runs once. Measure it and weep. 2/5

CTEs for readability, temp tables for size.

WITH makes logic clear. Past six figures of rows, materialize and index instead. 3/5

Paginate with keyset, not OFFSET.

WHERE id > last_id LIMIT 100 stays fast on page 10,000. OFFSET rescans everything. 4/5

IF YOU WANT TO DEBUG SLOW QUERIES FAST, STOP GUESSING.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 CHECKS: 1/5

Run EXPLAIN first, always.

Seq scan on a big table is your prime suspect. The plan tells you where time goes. 2/5

Check for missing indexes on JOIN keys.

Unindexed foreign keys turn joins into nested loops from hell. 3/5

Watch for N+1 hiding in ORMs.

One query per parent plus one per child. Eager load or batch it and watch latency collapse. 4/5
